newsitem.title: UK: Daily Mail lifts profits eight percent.
newsitem.headline: Daily Mail lifts profits eight percent.

text.p: Britain's Daily Mail and General Trust Plc, publishers of the national daily newspaper The Daily Mail, on Thursday reported an eight percent increase in full year profits before tax and exceptional items to 85.5 million pounds ($141.7 million).
The company reported an exceptional item of 8.1 million related to reorganisation costs and redundancy.
Circulation of the Daily Mail rose 13 percent on average and by five percent on The Mail on Sunday while advertising revenue showed an overall rise of 10 percent.

Sales grew despite an increase in the cover prices of both newspapers in the previous financial year. The company's flagship Daily Mail newspaper now sells an average daily two million copies and costs 35p.

But profits were held back by a 37 percent rise in newsprint prices. Expenditure on raw materials, mostly newsprint, rose by 79 million pounds and amounts charged against trading profits for starting up businesses went up six million to 23 million.
Daily Mail shares were off 7-1/2p at 1255p in early trade.

The group began operating radio stations for the first time during the year after the acquisition of a Stockholm station in March and more significantly with the purchase in September of a chain of 12 regional radio stations in Australia.
But the company said most of its businesses had started the new financial year well and the "first price reduction in newsprint has been achieved."
Advertising revenue in the Northcliffe titles have shown "particular strength, although some of Associated's display advertising categories have been weaker of late," it said.
The company's newspapers turned in profits of 82.9 million up from 74.3 million, its subsidiary Euromoney Publications increased trading profit by 4.9 million to 22 million.
But losses from the group's television activities, again centred around cable Channel One, were a little higher than expected due to the slow expansion of cable subscribers.
Its other media division reported a loss of 8.9 million down from an 11.5 million loss last time.
But it said some disposals are also being made, notably of the group's investment in Westcountry Television, which are likely to generate gains of at least 15 million in the 1996-97 results.

The groups borrowings at September 29, 1996 were 424 million, an increase of 208 million during the year. A total of 210 milion was spent on acquisitions and 36 million on capital expenditure. The company's interest charge rose from 10.5 million to 27.3 million. ($1=.6034 Pound)
